deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can destroy the queue. Using PREVENT for protected queues reduces the risk of accidental or unauthorised removal of task-processing infrastructure.

desired_state.description:
The desired state of the queue. Use this to pause and resume the queue.

* RUNNING: The queue is running. Tasks can be dispatched.
* PAUSED: The queue is paused. Tasks are not dispatched but can be added to the queue. Default value: "RUNNING" Possible values: ["RUNNING", "PAUSED"]
desired_state.rationale: Controls whether the queue is running or paused. This is primarily an operational state setting, and neither RUNNING nor PAUSED is inherently insecure without workload context.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.rationale: Identifies the queue. The queue name does not itself control authentication, authorisation, encryption, network access, or task execution security.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Selects the Google Cloud project containing the queue. Security of the project is governed primarily through IAM and project-level controls, and there is no universally secure project identifier for this resource.

app_engine_routing_override.description:
Overrides for task-level appEngineRouting. These settings apply only
to App Engine tasks in this queue

app_engine_routing_override.instance.description:
App instance.

By default, the task is sent to an instance which is available when the task is attempted.
app_engine_routing_override.instance.rationale: Selects an App Engine instance for routing. Whether an instance is appropriate or secure depends on the application deployment, so no generic platform-wide secure value can be defined.

app_engine_routing_override.service.description:
App service.

By default, the task is sent to the service which is the default service when the task is attempted.
app_engine_routing_override.service.rationale: Selects the App Engine service used for task routing. This is application-specific routing configuration, and no service name is inherently secure or insecure across all deployments.

app_engine_routing_override.version.description:
App version.

By default, the task is sent to the version which is the default version when the task is attempted.
app_engine_routing_override.version.rationale: Selects an App Engine version for task routing. The security of a version depends on the deployed application and patch state rather than the version identifier itself.

http_target.description: Modifies HTTP target for HTTP tasks.

http_target.http_method.description:
The HTTP method to use for the request.

When specified, it overrides HttpRequest for the task.
Note that if the value is set to GET the body of the task will be ignored at execution time. Possible values: ["HTTP_METHOD_UNSPECIFIED", "POST", "GET", "HEAD", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH", "OPTIONS"]
http_target.http_method.rationale: Overrides the HTTP method used by tasks. Methods such as POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE can all be legitimate depending on the application, so there is no universal secure method policy for every queue.

http_target.header_overrides.description:
HTTP target headers.

This map contains the header field names and values.
Headers will be set when running the CreateTask and/or BufferTask.

These headers represent a subset of the headers that will be configured for the task's HTTP request.
Some HTTP request headers will be ignored or replaced.

Headers which can have multiple values (according to RFC2616) can be specified using comma-separated values.

The size of the headers must be less than 80KB. Queue-level headers to override headers of all the tasks in the queue.

http_target.header_overrides.header.description: Header embodying a key and a value.

http_target.header_overrides.header.key.rationale: Defines an application-specific HTTP header name. Whether a header is security-sensitive depends on the receiving application and request design, so it cannot be generically classified from the key alone.

http_target.header_overrides.header.valu.rationale: Contains an application-specific HTTP header value. Its security meaning depends on the associated header and receiving application, so arbitrary values cannot be classified generically as secure or insecure.

http_target.oauth_token.description:
If specified, an OAuth token is generated and attached as the Authorization header in the HTTP request.

This type of authorization should generally be used only when calling Google APIs hosted on *.googleapis.com.
Note that both the service account email and the scope MUST be specified when using the queue-level authorization override.

http_target.oauth_token.scope.description:
OAuth scope to be used for generating OAuth access token.
If not specified, "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" will be used.
http_target.oauth_token.scope.rationale: Controls the OAuth scope used when generating access tokens for task requests. Restricting scopes supports least privilege and reduces the permissions available to generated credentials.

http_target.oauth_token.service_account_.description:
Service account email to be used for generating OAuth token.
The service account must be within the same project as the queue.
The caller must have iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permission for the service account.
http_target.oauth_token.service_account_.rationale: Determines the service account identity used to generate OAuth access tokens. Restricting this value to approved service accounts helps prevent tasks from operating under unintended identities or privileges.

http_target.oidc_token.description:
If specified, an OIDC token is generated and attached as an Authorization header in the HTTP request.

This type of authorization can be used for many scenarios, including calling Cloud Run, or endpoints where you intend to validate the token yourself.
Note that both the service account email and the audience MUST be specified when using the queue-level authorization override.

http_target.oidc_token.audience.description: Audience to be used when generating OIDC token. If not specified, the URI specified in target will be used.
http_target.oidc_token.audience.rationale: Defines the intended audience of generated OIDC tokens. Restricting the audience to approved targets supports token recipient validation and reduces the risk of tokens being issued for unintended services.

http_target.oidc_token.service_account_e.description:
Service account email to be used for generating OIDC token.
The service account must be within the same project as the queue.
The caller must have iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permission for the service account.
http_target.oidc_token.service_account_e.rationale: Determines the service account identity represented by generated OIDC tokens. Restricting this value to approved identities supports least privilege and controlled workload authentication.

http_target.uri_override.description:
URI override.

When specified, overrides the execution URI for all the tasks in the queue.

http_target.uri_override.host.description:
Host override.

When specified, replaces the host part of the task URL.
For example, if the task URL is "https://www.google.com", and host value
is set to "example.net", the overridden URI will be changed to "https://example.net".
Host value cannot be an empty string (INVALID_ARGUMENT).
http_target.uri_override.host.rationale: Replaces the host component of the execution URI for tasks in the queue. Restricting host overrides to approved destinations can prevent task traffic from being redirected to unintended or untrusted endpoints.

http_target.uri_override.port.description:
Port override.

When specified, replaces the port part of the task URI.
For instance, for a URI http://www.google.com/foo and port=123, the overridden URI becomes http://www.google.com:123/foo.
Note that the port value must be a positive integer.
Setting the port to 0 (Zero) clears the URI port.
http_target.uri_override.port.rationale: Overrides the destination port used by task requests. Appropriate ports depend on the target application's architecture, so there is no universal secure port value for all Cloud Tasks queues.

http_target.uri_override.scheme.description:
Scheme override.

When specified, the task URI scheme is replaced by the provided value (HTTP or HTTPS). Possible values: ["HTTP", "HTTPS"]
http_target.uri_override.scheme.rationale: Controls whether the overridden task URI uses HTTP or HTTPS. Enforcing HTTPS provides transport encryption and reduces exposure of task traffic to interception or modification in transit.

http_target.uri_override.uri_override_en.description:
URI Override Enforce Mode

When specified, determines the Target UriOverride mode. If not specified, it defaults to ALWAYS. Possible values: ["ALWAYS", "IF_NOT_EXISTS"]
http_target.uri_override.uri_override_en.rationale: Controls when URI overrides are applied. Both ALWAYS and IF_NOT_EXISTS can be valid depending on how task-level routing is managed, so neither value is inherently insecure.

http_target.uri_override.path_override.description:
URI path.

When specified, replaces the existing path of the task URL.
Setting the path value to an empty string clears the URI path segment.

http_target.uri_override.path_override.p.description: The URI path (e.g., /users/1234). Default is an empty string.
http_target.uri_override.path_override.p.rationale: Replaces the application-specific URI path used for task execution. Secure path values depend on the target application's endpoint design and cannot be defined generically at platform level.

http_target.uri_override.query_override.description:
URI query.

When specified, replaces the query part of the task URI. Setting the query value to an empty string clears the URI query segment.

http_target.uri_override.query_override..description: The query parameters (e.g., qparam1=123&qparam2=456). Default is an empty string.
http_target.uri_override.query_override..rationale: Replaces application-specific URI query parameters. Their meaning and security impact depend on the receiving application, so generic platform-level validation would be overly application-specific.

rate_limits.description:
Rate limits for task dispatches.

The queue's actual dispatch rate is the result of:

* Number of tasks in the queue
* User-specified throttling: rateLimits, retryConfig, and the queue's state.
* System throttling due to 429 (Too Many Requests) or 503 (Service
  Unavailable) responses from the worker, high error rates, or to
  smooth sudden large traffic spikes.

rate_limits.max_concurrent_dispatches.description:
The maximum number of concurrent tasks that Cloud Tasks allows to
be dispatched for this queue. After this threshold has been
reached, Cloud Tasks stops dispatching tasks until the number of
concurrent requests decreases.
rate_limits.max_concurrent_dispatches.rationale: Controls queue throughput by limiting concurrent task dispatches. This is primarily a capacity and reliability setting, and an appropriate value depends on downstream service capacity rather than a universal security baseline.

rate_limits.max_dispatches_per_second.description:
The maximum rate at which tasks are dispatched from this queue.

If unspecified when the queue is created, Cloud Tasks will pick the default.
rate_limits.max_dispatches_per_second.rationale: Controls the maximum rate at which tasks are dispatched. This is primarily a throttling and performance setting whose appropriate value depends on workload and downstream capacity.

retry_config.description: Settings that determine the retry behavior.

retry_config.max_attempts.description:
Number of attempts per task.

Cloud Tasks will attempt the task maxAttempts times (that is, if
the first attempt fails, then there will be maxAttempts - 1
retries). Must be >= -1.

If unspecified when the queue is created, Cloud Tasks will pick
the default.

-1 indicates unlimited attempts.
retry_config.max_attempts.rationale: Controls how many times failed tasks are attempted. Although excessive retries can affect resource usage, this setting primarily defines retry behaviour and its appropriate value depends on workload reliability requirements.

retry_config.max_backoff.description:
A task will be scheduled for retry between minBackoff and
maxBackoff duration after it fails, if the queue's RetryConfig
specifies that the task should be retried.
retry_config.max_backoff.rationale: Controls the maximum delay between retries. The appropriate value depends on workload recovery requirements, making this a reliability parameter rather than a universal security control.

retry_config.max_doublings.description:
The time between retries will double maxDoublings times.

A task's retry interval starts at minBackoff, then doubles maxDoublings times,
then increases linearly, and finally retries retries at intervals of maxBackoff
up to maxAttempts times.
retry_config.max_doublings.rationale: Controls how many times the retry interval increases exponentially. This is retry scheduling behaviour rather than an independent security control.

retry_config.max_retry_duration.description:
If positive, maxRetryDuration specifies the time limit for
retrying a failed task, measured from when the task was first
attempted. Once maxRetryDuration time has passed and the task has
been attempted maxAttempts times, no further attempts will be
made and the task will be deleted.

If zero, then the task age is unlimited.
retry_config.max_retry_duration.rationale: Controls how long failed tasks remain eligible for retries. The appropriate duration depends on workload and recovery requirements, so no generic secure duration applies to all queues.

retry_config.min_backoff.description:
A task will be scheduled for retry between minBackoff and
maxBackoff duration after it fails, if the queue's RetryConfig
specifies that the task should be retried.
retry_config.min_backoff.rationale: Controls the minimum delay before retrying failed tasks. Appropriate retry timing depends on downstream capacity and workload behaviour, making this primarily an operational reliability setting.

stackdriver_logging_config.description: Configuration options for writing logs to Stackdriver Logging.

stackdriver_logging_config.sampling_rati.description:
Specifies the fraction of operations to write to Stackdriver Logging.
This field may contain any value between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive. 0.0 is the
default and means that no operations are logged.
stackdriver_logging_config.sampling_rati.rationale: Controls the fraction of queue operations written to Cloud Logging. A value of 0.0 disables operation logging, so requiring a non-zero sampling level supports security monitoring, investigation, and audit visibility.
